szoveg_eredeti:
Nurses' Clinical Reasoning Competency Linked to Higher Artificial Intelligence Literacy in China

A cross-sectional investigation conducted among registered nurses in China has revealed that stronger clinical reasoning competency is significantly associated with higher artificial intelligence literacy. As clinical environments increasingly integrate machine intelligence into routine workflows, the findings suggest that foundational reasoning abilities may play a vital role in how healthcare professionals comprehend, evaluate, and employ digital tools in practice.

The study, published in BMC Nursing, grounded its inquiry in Cognitive Load Theory to examine how health practitioners handle automated systems. Within this conceptual framework, information generated by artificial intelligence tools can substantially increase the cognitive demands placed on clinicians during patient care. Investigators proposed that advanced clinical reasoning skills might assist healthcare workers in organizing and synthesizing this complex digital output, thereby establishing a meaningful link with their overall technical literacy.

To evaluate these dynamics, researchers recruited a convenience sample comprising 306 registered nurses stationed across healthcare institutions in Guangdong Province, China. Information was gathered via the professional online platform SO JUMP.28. The data collection protocol captured participants’ sociodemographic profiles alongside standardized evaluations from the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale and the Nurse Clinical Reasoning Scale.

Statistical evaluation of the dataset involved both nonparametric tests and regression modeling to examine patterns across participant cohorts. Analysts utilized descriptive statistics, the Mann-Whitney U test, and the Kruskal-Wallis H test to assess subgroup variations. Relationships between measured dimensions were further explored using Spearman’s rank correlation alongside multiple linear regression modeling.

Assessment of overall literacy revealed that participating nurses achieved a median total score of 90.00 on the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale, with an interquartile range extending from 79.00 to 97.00. Bivariate analysis demonstrated that each distinct dimension of artificial intelligence literacy maintained a statistically significant positive correlation with clinical reasoning competency, yielding correlation coefficients ranging from r = 0.289 to r = 0.551, with significance levels reaching P < 0.001 across all measured aspects.

When confounding background factors were accounted for in a multivariable linear regression model, clinical reasoning competency remained independently associated with artificial intelligence literacy, displaying a standardized coefficient of beta = 0.509 (P < 0.001). The regression analysis additionally identified the participant’s highest educational degree as a distinct independent factor, producing a standardized coefficient of beta = 0.111 (P = 0.047) after controlling for sociodemographic variables.

The research team concluded that clinical reasoning competency represents an essential cognitive attribute linked directly to proficiency in handling intelligent systems. By demonstrating an empirical connection between cognitive clinical processing and technological literacy, the authors underscored that ongoing nurse training curricula and artificial intelligence instructional programs should address clinical reasoning capabilities alongside direct technical instruction.

Subject of Research: Association between artificial intelligence literacy and clinical reasoning competency among registered nurses

Article Title: Association between artificial intelligence literacy and clinical reasoning competency among nurses: a cross-sectional study

Article References: Yang, M., Lu, J., Peng, Y., Zheng, Y., Liao, Z., Hu, X., Yuan, J., Lin, Z., Li, R., & Hu, Y. (2026). Association between artificial intelligence literacy and clinical reasoning competency among nurses: a cross-sectional study. BMC Nursing. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12912-026-05598-5

Keywords: artificial intelligence literacy, clinical reasoning competency, nursing research, Cognitive Load Theory, registered nurses, Guangdong Province, cross-sectional study, healthcare AI, Nurse Clinical Reasoning Scale, Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale, multiple linear regression, nursing education, clinical decision-making, Spearman correlation, health informatics, professional development
